chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Bakr ibn Abi Bakr who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I sometimes doubt regarding the Surah, so I do not know if I recited it or not, should I repeat it?' He said: 'If it is long, do not (repeat it); and if it is short, then repeat it.'

key_terms.طَوِيلَةً: Long (referring to the length of the Surah)
key_terms.قَصِيرَةً: Short (referring to the length of the Surah)

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they doubt whether they recited a Surah during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a practical distinction in the fiqh of doubt (shakk) during prayer, differentiating between long and short Surahs to balance ritual completeness with ease. It reflects the Shia scholarly approach of applying leniency to avoid excessive burden, where the brevity of short Surahs makes repetition negligible, whereas the length of long ones makes repetition a significant disruption. This ruling underscores the principle of *sahh* (validity) over *i'tidal* (perfection) when doubt arises in obligatory recitation.
